subject: Quantitative GPU runbook & soft-reserve — Cobra Technologies
body:
---Message 1 (2028-06-30 09:12 PDT)---
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Subject: Quantitative GPU runbook & soft-reserve — Cobra Technologies

Team,

Cobra is in final commercial review (DEAL-7831). They plan a GA launch in Q4 and asked for a non-binding capacity earmark to avoid compute scarcity during ramp. Legal is close on commercial terms; procurement asked that we hold inventory for a 30-day pre-commit window while contracts are routed.

High level from the customer & product:
- Model: Llama-2-70B-chat variant (2-stage: generate + rerank).
- Expected steady-state: ~220 qps inference requests at 512 token avg per request during 2 peak hours/day.
- P0 SLO: 95th percentile latency < 150ms per request.
- They want H100 preferred due to perf for their reranker.

Ask: can infra/ops evaluate whether we can place a soft-reserve (non-binding) on ~H100/A100 nodes in us-west region for a 30–45 day hold window and give a sizing recommendation (GA headroom vs conservative), plus clear fallback plan (quantized variant, fallback model smaller).

If possible please attach a quick calc sheet and call out delivery risk (thermal/maintenance windows) and whether this affects any other late-stage pipeline.

Attached: I will attach a working calc once Ben fills numbers.

Thanks —
Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
---

---Message 2 (2028-06-30 10:05 PDT)---
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Quantitative GPU runbook & soft-reserve — Cobra Technologies

Steph + team —

Quick sizing draft (rough):
- Baseline perf observed internally for Llama-2-70B-chat: H100 (full-precision, batch 8): ~75 tokens/sec per GPU for our optimized runtime; A100-80GB: ~42 tokens/sec.
- Cobra's 220 qps * 512 tokens ~= 112k tokens/sec incoming. Accounting for batching and concurrency, realistic steady-state token throughput needed: ~120k tokens/sec.

Sizing options (headroom assumptions included):
1) Preferred (latency-first, H100): 12 x H100 (expected aggregate ~900 tokens/sec per GPU cluster? Wait check math). Let me calculate clearly: if H100 does 75 tokens/sec per GPU PER REQUEST? Need to reframe: our measured throughput is tokens/sec per GPU when fully utilized. So per-GPU token/sec = 75k? Hmm.

I'm attaching cobra_capacity_calc.xlsx with two scenarios: H100-primary and mixed fleet (A100 fallback). In brief: H100-primary requires fewer nodes — recommended soft-reserve: 10 H100 nodes for 30 days as a safety buffer (covers peak + 25% buffer). Mixed fleet fallback: 18 A100-80GB nodes (higher count due to lower perf).

Notes:
- A conservative procurement ask to ops: place a soft-reserve of 10 H100-equivalent GPUs in us-west (non-binding hold, release on signature or re-plan).
- Cost/commit: estimate monthly committed-GPU-hours if they convert — see sheet.

Attaching the calc and a brief checklist.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: cobra_capacity_calc.xlsx
---

---Message 3 (2028-07-01 11:38 PDT)---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Quantitative GPU runbook & soft-reserve — Cobra Technologies

Thanks Ben — I pulled the numbers with the runtime team and clarified throughput units. Clarifications and recs below.

Clarifications:
- Our runtime metric is tokens/sec per GPU for steady autoregressive generation. For Llama-2-70B-chat at 512 tokens average using our optimized kernel path: H100 (FP16/AMP) ~= 110k tokens/sec per GPU when fully batched; A100-80GB ~= 62k tokens/sec. (Ben's draft used per-thread numbers.)

Recalculating:
- Required tokens/sec ~= 220 qps * 512 tokens = 112,640 tokens/sec.
- H100 nodes required (no headroom) = 112,640 / 110,000 ~= 1.03 -> effectively 2 GPUs for steady throughput if perfectly batched. But latency SLO and less-than-perfect batching demand headroom.

Operational sizing (recommended):
- Latency-first profile (95th <150ms): recommend 8 x H100 (provides 3–4x headroom for peaks, allows for maintenance or transient load spikes).
- Cost-conservative profile: 16 x A100-80GB (gives comparable headroom but more nodes).

Additional engineering notes:
- We must reserve KV cache memory for chat context; that reduces effective per-GPU tokens/sec by ~10–15% for long conversations. Plan for that in final calc.
- We have an autoscaling policy that can add burst H100 capacity from pooled spot resources, but spot cannot be guaranteed during initial customer ramp; soft-reserve should target reserved instances.

Request to Kimberly: can you confirm node counts available in us-west for the July window (30–45 days) and whether we can set a soft hold on 8 H100s with ops tagging to keep them off general allocation? Also flag any other deals that would conflict.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Capacity Planning Lead | Redwood Inference
---

---Message 4 (2028-07-02 08:21 PDT)---
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@cobra-tech.com>
Cc: ops@cobra-tech.com, procurement@cobra-tech.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Quantitative GPU runbook & soft-reserve — Cobra Technologies

Elena —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per our internal sizing review: Redwood recommends a non-binding soft-reserve of 8 H100 nodes in us-west (30-day window) to cover expected peaks and give a clean onboarding runway. If you want a cost-optimized fallback we can instead earmark 16 A100-80GB nodes.

What the soft-reserve means (non-binding):
- Redwood will tag and hold 8 H100 nodes in us-west and not allocate them to other on-demand customers.
- This hold is non-billable and non-binding for 30 days; it simply reduces risk while your procurement and legal finalize terms.
- If the contract signs within the window, we convert the hold into the agreed reserved capacity and finalize billing/commitment starting at activation.

Next steps (to keep moving):
1) Cobra procurement to confirm preference (H100 or A100 fallback) and provide an internal PO target date.
2) Redwood ops (Kimberly & Marcus) to confirm availability and put a soft-reserve tag.
3) We will share a short preflight checklist and a DocuSign for the reserved-capacity amendment once procurement signals green.

I attached the capacity calc and our preflight checklist for transparency.

Are you comfortable with the 8 H100 soft-reserve for 30 days? If you'd like the 45-day window we can discuss.

Best,
Steph
---

---Message 5 (2028-07-03 15:06 PDT)---
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@cobra-tech.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cobra-tech.com, procurement@cobra-tech.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Quantitative GPU runbook & soft-reserve — Cobra Technologies

Hi Steph, Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary and the calc. Cobra is comfortable with the 8 H100 non-binding soft-reserve for 30 days while procurement finalizes the PO. A couple of asks from our side:
- Procurement will need the estimated committed-GPU-hours and indicative monthly cost (Ben's calc covered this; can you surface a 1-page summary for the PO pack?).
- Technical ask: Cobra's latency target is 95th <120ms. Are there toggles (quantization to 4-bit + KV cache tuning) that preserve accuracy but help latency headroom if we need to drop to A100s mid-launch?

Please confirm the soft-reserve is tagged today if possible, and share the short 1-page PO-friendly cost summary plus the DocuSign stub for the reserve-amendment. Procurement is aiming to sign within 21 days.

Regards,
Elena Ruiz
VP Product, Cobra Technologies
